Kubrick's final film Eyes Wide Shut, like so many of his previous works, was released to a somewhat lukewarm reception. However, it has increasingly gained acclaim throughout the 15 years after its initial release. It still remains a haunting and mesmerising final piece, the last message of a master to the world. What are your thoughts on Eyes Wide Shut? What message do you think it conveyed? Any interesting theories?

I have seen every one of Kubrick’s films, including his first, “Fear and Desire” which I happened to enjoy even though he worked hard to suppress it. Several of his films I have seen more than once and count myself an admirer of Kubrick as a filmmaker. With that said, I found “Eyes Wide Shut” to be the only film in his body of work a great disappointment. I have seen it twice thinking I may have overlooked something here or there but in doing so I have concluded that my distaste with the film has to do primarily with the casting of Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman as the leads. They are no doubt very beautiful people but they lack sophistication and neither of them are good actors and so watching their performances was painful viewing for me.

Like “Barry Lyndon,” “Eyes Wide Shut” appears to be one of two films that were very personal for Kubrick. Lyndon, however, was an artistic exercise that did something I had never seen before – bringing paintings to life. It is literally a film about motion pictures.

“Eyes Wide Shut,” on the other hand, was lit similarly to “The Shining” and retained a Kubrick feel visually, but, I found the storyline weak and the characters cold and impersonal; so I really didn’t care about them or their relationship. I rank Kubrick as one of the best filmmakers in history so it bothers me that I dislike his final film as much as I do. I may watch it again, but I'll probably need a drink or two before putting up with Cruise’s insufferable performance again.
I thought that the lighting in Eyes Wide Shut was really beautiful... I'm not usually into technical aspects of movies,but I've watched the movie again just to see how amazing the lighting looks
Agreed. Visually Eyes Wide Shut is beautiful. The ballroom scenes in that film remind me of the bar in The Shining. Same kind of lighting.

You're right, the lighting in 'Eyes Wide Shut' was similar to 'The Shining,' particularly the Gold Room scenes with Jack. Although, I agree that 'Eyes Wide Shut' isn't Kubrick's best film, it's still a great film with a lot of great qualities in my opinion. I think the story might have seemed simple on the surface but it had a lot of complex undertones and references. Kubrick incorporated quite a lot of steganography in all his films which usually goes unnoticed by majority of viewers the first time they watch his films.

I also found the themes of the film really interesting: Lust, symbolic masks worn by the characters, the wealthy elite, and secret societies just to name a few. Bill Harford character going on this mysterious midnight sex odyssey through colorfully lit streets after his wife bruises his ego was really mesmerizing to me. His character in the beginning is shown to be shallow, egotistical and he always resorts to using his money to get what he wants but after his ordeal at the mansion, he is humbled. Albeit Cruise's acting wasn't the best, it certainly wasn't bad in my opinion and it didn't take me out of the mood of the film.
